notes: Heating mode: the indoor coil is the condenser and the outdoor coil the evaporator. Cooling superheat/subcooling charging charts do NOT apply; charge by the manufacturer heating check chart (discharge or liquid pressure vs outdoor DB and indoor DB) or weigh in the nameplate charge after recovery and evacuation.

Typical heating targets (verify against the unit chart): indoor coil temperature difference (condensing sat minus indoor entering DB) 25-35 F; outdoor coil TD (outdoor DB minus evaporating sat) 15-30 F, shrinking as frost builds; temperature rise across the indoor coil 20-35 F at rated airflow (much less below ~30 F outdoor); compressor superheat 5-15 F at the accumulator outlet.

Suction pressure in heating must be read at the compressor suction / accumulator outlet port, NOT at the vapor service valve on the outdoor unit: in heating that valve carries hot discharge gas to the indoor coil.
Frost on the outdoor coil, an active or recent defrost (within ~10 min), or outdoor DB below ~20 F make gauge readings unusable for charge; readings taken during defrost look like a cooling cycle.

Many manufacturers publish a heating check chart for verification only; if the chart is unavailable, weigh-in (nameplate charge plus line-set adder) is the only reliable method. When in doubt, wait for cooling-season conditions (outdoor DB 65 F or more) to charge by subcooling/superheat.
Reversing valve leak-by in heating shows as discharge superheat under ~30 F with high suction pressure and more than 3-4 F between the suction line and the reversing valve's suction-side tube.
Nameplate and manufacturer charging charts always take precedence over these generic tables. Use these only when the unit chart is unavailable, and say so in the write-up.

fixedOrificeSuperheat follows the standard field 'required superheat' chart used by Carrier/Bryant, Goodman/Amana, Rheem and Trane for fixed-orifice (piston, capillary tube) systems: rows = indoor entering wet bulb (50-76 F, 2 F steps), columns = outdoor entering dry bulb (55-115 F, 5 F steps), value = total superheat at the outdoor unit suction service valve, F. null = charging not recommended at those conditions (the chart bottoms out below 5 F superheat: add heat to the space or wait for a higher indoor load).

Fixed-orifice charging: measure superheat at the outdoor unit (suction pressure and suction line temperature about 6 in. from the service valve); compare to the chart; adjust charge in small steps and wait 10-15 minutes between adjustments. Tolerance +/- 3-5 F. Do not charge below 55 F outdoor (many charts stop at 60-65 F). Never add refrigerant without a leak check and valid readings.

TXV/EEV systems: charge by subcooling to the nameplate target (typically 8-15 F; default 10 F when unknown) with evaporator superheat 8-12 F and total superheat at the compressor 10-25 F. Do not blame the TXV until subcooling is right and airflow is verified.

targetDeltaT follows the Carrier 'cooling delta-T / evaporator temperature drop' chart style: rows = evaporator entering dry bulb, columns = entering wet bulb, value = expected supply-air temperature drop (F) at rated airflow (~400 CFM/ton). Humid air (high WB for the DB) gives a smaller sensible delta-T because more capacity goes to latent load; dry air gives a larger drop. Reference points: 75/63 -> ~19, 75/58 -> ~23, 75/68 -> ~14. null where WB is at or above DB (not physical) or the drop is below the chart range. Expect +/- 3 F on a field reading.

Delta-T is a capacity/airflow sanity check, not a charging method. Low delta-T: high airflow, humid air, low capacity (charge, compressor, restriction); high delta-T: low airflow (filters, coil, belts, ESP, closed dampers).

Refrigeration targets (medium-temp walk-in/reach-in, ~25-35 F box with 10-12 F evaporator TD; low-temp freezer -10 to 0 F box with 6-10 F TD): evaporator superheat 6-10 F at the coil outlet, total superheat 20-30 F at the compressor (more with long suction lines), condenser split 20-30 F air-cooled, compression ratio normally 4-8 medium temp and 8-12 low temp; discharge line under 225 F. Charge by sight glass only with a subcooled liquid line and normal head pressure; at low ambient a bubbling glass while head-pressure control cycles is normal.

Low-ambient cooling operation (outdoor DB below 65 F): head-pressure control (fan cycling, fan VFD/Motormaster, or a flooding/condenser holdback valve) should hold condensing saturation about 90-105 F. Without confirmed head-pressure control, do not evaluate charge from gauge readings below 65 F outdoor. Flooding valves hold extra charge in the condenser: high subcooling alone is not overcharge on such systems; use the manufacturer winter charge table.
Elevation: field gauge readings drop about 0.5 psi per 1,000 ft; the engine corrects them to sea-level basis before PT lookup when elevationFt is supplied.

Sources followed: Carrier residential/commercial cooling charging charts (superheat and subcooling methods), Goodman/Amana superheat charging table (fixed orifice), Trane and Lennox charging procedures, Copeland AE-series application bulletins (discharge temperature, floodback, compression ratio), RSES/ESCO refrigeration troubleshooting charts. Values are generic and rounded; unit-specific charts win.
